title: Vendor, code-object family, lowering route and allocation are four axes, and shared code keeps collapsing them into a target id enumerated by hand

evidence.note: The device survey that separates the axes on one machine: rocminfo reports vendor C-3000 and device type HCU, Triton registers an hcu backend beside amd and selects it, the FP16 dot lowers to v_mmac_f32_16x16x16_f16 rather than any v_mfma, dcc 25.10.0's llc names gfx926/928/936/938 beside the AMD CPUs, and the host installs hy-smi and rocm-smi and no amd-smi -- while the object it emits still carries the amdgcn-amd-amdhsa-- triple. One device, three different answers depending on which axis is being asked about.

The Executor host capture that found two of the instances below: the HIP host contract pinned amd-smi as the device monitor where this host installs rocm-smi and hy-smi, and required a --version probe that rocprof answers with exit 1 and its run banner for --version, -v and --help alike. Both refused the host rather than the tool.

The first real --baseline-only launch for triton-dcu, which is what found the allocation axis. It refused at the allocator with "Triton execution requires the existing gpu-run allocator" before reaching any DCU-specific code, then after the split advanced to the stale Executor closure refusal naming src/open_cake_ir/tasks/devices.py -- the expected consequence of changing a pinned runtime source, not a new defect.

The first sealed DCU baseline, built through `launch_task.py --baseline-only` in the DTK container: a 5800-byte HSACO beside 19 KB of AMDGCN assembly, and a launch manifest declaring block [64,1,1] -- one wave64 -- grid [128,1,1] and one hidden scratch pointer, which is the AMDGCN scratch count the route declares and confirms that reading it off the route rather than the CUDA literal 2 was correct.

observation:
Eight separate repairs in one bring-up, and they are the same defect. Shared code keeps deciding a per-target question by enumerating target ids, and the enumerations disagree about which question they are answering. Measured in this checkout: Target.warp_size was one constant for every target, closed upstream in Compiler v81. warps_per_warpgroup and every vendor-keyed rule read the presence of compute_capability, so a well-formed non-CUDA document was refused in CUDA's words and a fabricated capability pair made it parse with a borrowed 32-lane width. A host declared `kind` for Metal and `runtime_kind` for HIP. The schema v2 Executor identity was a gfx1151 literal, which refuses gfx938 for being the wrong vendor's target when the two differ by vendor and agree on the code object. gfx938 was declared vendor amd on Hygon hardware. evaluation/artifacts.py holds METAL_TARGETS, _CUBIN_TARGETS and AMDGCN_TARGETS -- three frozensets of target ids partitioning all seven targets by code object, read from six sites across evaluation and lab, none of which any Target document can state. The HIP host contract pinned amd-smi as the device monitor and a --version interface that rocprof does not have. Underneath all eight: vendor (who built the hardware), code-object family (what the compiled artifact is) and lowering route (which mechanism emits source) are three independent axes. gfx938 and gfx1151 share a code object and differ by vendor; sm_100a and gfx938 share neither but both reach Triton; apple_gpu_family9 and sm_100a share a lane width and nothing else. Declaring one axis and inferring the rest is what produced every instance above. A ninth instance arrived after this finding was written, and it is a fourth axis. tools/launch_task.py read the allocator off the lowering route: a triton route took the gpu-run CUDA cluster allocator, a metal route took the local broker. That held while every Triton target was a B200. A Hygon DCU lowers through Triton and is reached like an Apple device -- one visible device, no cluster allocator -- so the launch refused it with "Triton execution requires the existing gpu-run allocator", naming a NVIDIA cluster allocator a DCU has no use for. Allocation is independent of route for the same reason the other three are independent of each other, and it is now a declared column in tasks/devices.py rather than a consequence of the route. A tenth, smaller, in the same file: the isolated Triton build's jail was the constant "/usr/bin/bwrap", which is a fact about the distributions this route was built against, not about bubblewrap; a container that puts it elsewhere failed inside resolve(strict=True) naming a path nobody on that host chose.

The process lesson is separate from the axes and cost more than any single one of them. An eight-gate readiness checklist was written for the DCU Lab run and reached 7/8 -- and it had no gate for either of the two above, because every gate it did have asked about the compile chain: does the Target admit, does Triton select the backend, does the object parse, does the loader seal it. Nothing in it asked how a sealed candidate reaches a device. The first real --baseline-only run found that in one line. A checklist assembled from the failures already seen covers the layer those failures came from; running the real entry point is what names the next layer. Running the real entry point to completion found five more instances of the same defect, all of them behind the two already recorded and none of them in the compile chain the readiness checklist covered. The isolated build jail runs --clearenv, which is correct, and two DTK facts live only in /opt/dtk/env.sh: without LD_LIBRARY_PATH `import triton` fails with "libgalaxyhip.so.5: cannot open shared object file" while the file is mounted and present, and without ROCM_PATH clang-18 reports "cannot find ROCm device library". `TritonToolchainBuilder` named its artifact roles as the literals ptx and cubin while `triton_route` has carried `artifact_roles` per target all along, and wrote `hidden_null_pointer_parameters: 2` -- Triton's two CUDA scratch pointers -- where HIPOptions declares one, which would have sealed an ABI with a parameter the kernel does not take. `CudaKernelSpec.from_dict` resolved its target through `cuda_target`, whose first act is decoding an sm_1xxa capability, so a gfx938 manifest came back as "unsupported exact CUDA target" -- grid, block and shared-memory limits are declared by every Target document and none of them is CUDA's. `allowed_artifact_roles` returned the CUDA set for anything that was not Metal, so a candidate carrying the assembly and HSACO its own route produced was refused for not being PTX and a CUBIN. And the Study template chose its measurement source with `"metal" if metal else "cupti"`, so the first DCU study declared `fixed_baseline_paired_cupti_v1` on a machine with no CUPTI installed -- the exact outcome the comment on `_PAIRED_BACKENDS` warns about, arriving through the Study template rather than through that table. Five of those five are one shape: a per-target question answered by "is it Metal? otherwise CUDA".
proposed_change: Finish what warp_size and vendor started: make the code-object family a declared Target fact, and let the shared layers read it instead of enumerating ids. Concretely, a required Target field naming the object the target's toolchain produces -- cubin, metal_binary_archive, hsaco -- consumed by evaluation/artifacts.py's executable_role and _BUILD_ROLES in place of its three frozensets, and by the metal host, build and observation paths in place of their METAL_TARGETS membership tests. A new target then becomes a document, which is what AGENTS.md's registration rule says it should be, instead of a document plus six edits in Executor-pinned shared code. Leave the Compiler's offline tables alone: cuda_architecture and the AMDGCN route table are deliberate, because offline compilation must not open Target documents in its jail. What they must stop being is a second owner of a fact the document also states -- the route table carries a lane width the Target declares -- and the fix there is for the emitter, which holds the Target, to put that width in the toolchain requirements it already builds, rather than for the jail to look it up. That change alters the requirements contract every retained Triton candidate replays through, so it is sequenced after the declaration and not bundled with it. Until both land, the duplication is at least verified: a contract test holds the offline route's architecture and width against every declared AMDGCN Target document, so adding a target without updating the table fails rather than drifting. The allocation axis is already declared, so what remains for it is the same consolidation as the others: tasks/devices.py is now the single registry that states route, allocation, widths, dtypes and tanh contract per backend, and tasks/apple.py is a derived Metal-only view of it rather than a second list. Keep new per-target questions in that registry -- or better, in the Target document once the code-object field lands -- instead of in a fresh frozenset beside the existing three. For the jail: the Executor host is the right owner if anything is, but HIP_BUILD_TOOLS is a closed set with no bwrap in it, so every released descriptor is silent and discovery decides; pinning it is a capture-schema change that restales every HIP host and is not bundled here. Two of these are now declared facts rather than fall-throughs and are worth naming as the pattern to repeat: `runtime.build_environment` on a HIP host, which states the environment the jail must be given instead of one field per variable, and `timing_source` on a device registry row, where None is a real answer that makes the Study report a measurement-coverage limitation rather than inherit another target's timer. The remaining CUDA fall-through of this kind is `tasks/evaluate.py`, which dispatches on `MetalTensorLaunchManifest` and otherwise `observe_exclusive_cuda`.
implemented_in: the code-object declaration and the tasks/evaluate.py fall-through only: open-cake-ir@6951b5a67ba0eac00a2e3d842db1ade1ef707ff1 -- the merge that carried them to main on 2026-09-16. ADR 0065 makes the Revision the checkout's commit, and a commit cannot name itself, so the merge commit is what a backfill can name. The lane-width half and the jail item are not in it.
verification_plan: Capacity finding, verified by the absence its change is for: after the declaration lands, adding an eighth Target must require no edit to evaluation/artifacts.py, lab/metal_host.py, lab/metal_build.py, evaluation/metal_observations.py or lab/executor.py, and a neutrality test should assert that by constructing a synthetic target of a fourth vendor and reaching executable_role through the declared field alone. The lane-width half verifies by replaying retained Triton candidates through the successor requirements contract with unchanged compiled artifacts. Neither half claims a device result; both are shared-layer changes whose evidence is a Corpus Gate with unchanged expectations and the existing per-route contracts.

verified_by.scope: the code-object declaration and the tasks/evaluate.py CUDA fall-through this record names; not the lane-width half, which this record sequences after the declaration, and not the jail item it says is not bundled here
verified_by.observed: Every Target document declares code_object: cubin on sm_100a and sm_103a, metal_binary_archive on the three Apple families, hsaco on gfx938 and gfx1151. evaluation/artifacts.py's METAL_TARGETS, _CUBIN_TARGETS and AMDGCN_TARGETS are gone; executable_role and allowed_artifact_roles read the declaration, and lab/metal_host.py, lab/metal_build.py, evaluation/metal_observations.py and evaluation/metal_manifest.py ask whether the target declares a Metal archive instead of testing set membership. No target id remains in any of the five files this record's verification plan names. tasks/evaluate.py no longer dispatches on MetalTensorLaunchManifest: the path follows the declared object, the manifest and the declaration must agree with each other, and each object is a row in a registry rather than a branch. Making it a registry found a second fall-through this record did not name -- attribution had no platform test at all, so an AMDGCN candidate asking for a profile reached observe_exclusive_cuda and was refused by nvidia-smi, one branch below the one already named.
verified_by.contracts: tests/contracts/test_declared_code_object.py, which reaches executable_role for a synthetic fourth-vendor Target through the declared field alone, as this record's verification plan asks; and tests/contracts/test_execution_platform.py, which holds that every code object a Target declares has a platform row and that an object no platform implements is refused by name rather than falling through
verified_by.full_corpus_gate: 151/151 with every expectation unchanged, observed on main at de33397e
verified_by.limits: Two halves this record sequences are not implemented. The emitter still does not put the declared lane width in the toolchain requirements it builds, so compiler/toolchain.py's AMDGCN route table remains a second owner of that width, held against the declared documents by the existing contract test rather than retired; that change alters the requirements contract retained Triton candidates replay through, which is why this record sequences it separately. HIP_BUILD_TOOLS still carries no bwrap entry. No device result is claimed: every change here is in a shared layer and its evidence is a Corpus Gate with unchanged expectations and the per-route contracts. The decision field is left as written -- moving proposed to accepted is a review-path act, not the author's.
